response:
F001  
SEVERITY: 0.97  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.88  
DESCRIPTION: The adaptive routing loop is effectively broken. `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` claims to use live fingerprints, and `update_fingerprints()` updates `self._live_fingerprints`, but role reassignment uses `RoleAssignment._models`, which still contain the original static `ModelSpec.fingerprint` values. `RoleAssignment.reassign()` recomputes scores from those stale fingerprints, so dynamic capability adaptation never affects COL/PM/PAR ordering. This contradicts the module’s stated purpose of “adaptive routing feedback” and causes observed performance to have no effect on role assignment.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make role assignment read from live model specs/fingerprints rather than the original `_models`. Options: (a) update `RoleAssignment` to accept current `ModelSpec` list on `reassign()`, (b) have `DynamicManager` rebuild/recreate `RoleAssignment` from `get_live_models()`, preserving locked PM and failure history, or (c) store fingerprints separately and have `_capability_score` consult the live store.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F002  
SEVERITY: 0.94  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._solve_greedy()` can intentionally generate infeasible allocations by force-assigning a task even when it violates F1 (token capacity), while the class documentation says feasibility constraints F1/F2/F3 are HARD. `solve()` only emits a warning and returns the infeasible allocation. That is a correctness violation, not just a heuristic limitation, because callers may treat returned allocations as valid dispatch plans.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Do not return infeasible allocations as normal results. Either (a) raise an exception / return explicit infeasibility status, (b) relax redundancy first while preserving F1/F3, or (c) return partial allocation plus unmet-task set. HARD constraints should not be knowingly violated to preserve F2.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F003  
SEVERITY: 0.92  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: Pre-dispatch feasibility checking is not integrated into allocation or orchestration. `LoadBalancer.dispatch_check()` and `DynamicManager.check_dispatch_feasibility()` exist, but `get_allocation()` and `process_round()` never use them. The advertised Area 2 extension therefore does not affect actual scheduling decisions. Models can be allocated loads with low `P(feasible)` despite the stated threshold.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Integrate feasibility probability into allocation feasibility and/or objective. At minimum, filter candidate assignments where `P(feasible) < feasibility_threshold`; better, use it as a hard constraint during solving and emit events when assignments are pruned.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F004  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: In `FailureHandler.detect_failure()`, a format violation emits `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` instead of `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. This makes real-time monitoring semantically incorrect and prevents downstream consumers from distinguishing parse failures from formatting failures.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change the FORMAT branch to emit `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. Add a regression test asserting event type matches detected `FailureType`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F005  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` uses `same_type_count >= self.config.n_fail` before recording the current failure. With default `n_fail=2`, escalation happens on the third occurrence, not the second. The code comments in `validate_k1()` acknowledge this mismatch. This is an off-by-one error in the escalation policy.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define repetition consistently. If `n_fail` means “escalate on the nth occurrence,” use `(same_type_count + 1) >= n_fail`. Update docs/tests accordingly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F006  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: `CorrelatedFailureModel` is declared as `@dataclass` but lacks parentheses: `@dataclass` instead of `@dataclass()`. This is valid syntax, so not itself a bug. However, the class defines mutable fields with `field(default_factory=...)` and no explicit `__init__`; with `@dataclass` this is fine. No issue here.  
PROPOSED_FIX: None.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F007  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.kappa_adopt()` returns `1 - adoption_delta` without validation or clamping. If `adoption_delta` is outside [0,1], `kappa_adopt()` can be negative or greater than 1, violating its own documented range and contaminating `kappa()`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate/clamp `adoption_delta` on input in `add_round_findings()` or clamp in `kappa_adopt()` to [0,1]. Document accepted input domain.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F008  
SEVERITY: 0.85  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: `CapabilityFingerprint.as_normalised_array()` can produce negative values for the first component when `D_decay > pool_max[0]` or values outside the expected range if any fingerprint components exceed pool maxima due to inconsistent data. More fundamentally, there is no validation that fingerprint values lie in [0,1] where required. This can yield capability scores outside [0,1] despite docs claiming score range [0,1].  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `CapabilityFingerprint` fields in `__post_init__` (or equivalent factory) and clamp normalized values to [0,1]. Explicitly enforce allowed domains for `D_decay`, `v_bar`, `A`, and `C`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F009  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
DESCRIPTION: Configuration validation is incomplete. Only a few parameters are checked (`max_rounds`, `tau_kappa`, `feasibility_threshold`, alpha vector shape/sum). Many threshold-like values are undocumented as validated but can silently break semantics: `tau_sim`, `eta_veto`, `tau_mu`, `theta_under`, `eta_underperform`, `epsilon_rho`, `tau_critical`, `tau_moderate`, `fingerprint_ema_alpha`, etc. Invalid values can induce nonsensical behavior without fast failure.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Expand `DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__()` to validate all bounded parameters and cross-parameter invariants, e.g. `0<=tau_moderate<=tau_critical<=1`, `0<=tau_sim<=1`, `0<=fingerprint_ema_alpha<=1`, `n_fail>=1`, `persistence_window>=1`, `smoothing_window>=1`, `k_min>=1`, nonnegative costs/limits.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F010  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._redundancy_target()` uses `K = len(self.models)`, not the number of admissible/active non-PM models. For `K>1`, PM is excluded from standard tasks by `_admissibility_mask()`, yet high-criticality tasks target redundancy `K`, which may be impossible if PM is among `self.models`. This causes systematic unattainable redundancy targets and noisy infeasibility.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base redundancy targets on the number of admissible models for the task, not total model count. Compute target as min(policy_target, admissible_count).  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F011  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` uses `if len(self._models) >= 3:` to decide whether to assign a COL, instead of checking active model count. If the original pool had 3+ models but only two remain active (PM + one other), it still assigns a COL; if only one non-PM remains, that may be intended, but the stated initial assignment logic says COL is assigned “if K >= 3”, implying dependence on current pool size. Current behavior mixes original and active cardinality inconsistently.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use current active pool size for reassignment policy, and document whether PM+1 should yield COL or PAR only. Apply the same rule consistently in initial assignment and reassignment.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F012  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` assigns `flaw_class = members[0].flaw_class` even though cross-class merging is explicitly allowed when Jaccard exceeds `tau_sim`. That produces equivalence classes whose recorded `flaw_class` may disagree with some members, undermining any downstream logic assuming class purity.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either forbid cross-class merging, or represent class labels as a set/distribution of flaw classes, or choose a canonical label by majority and record mixed membership explicitly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F013  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: The convergence clustering uses single-linkage with thresholding, but novelty detection in `_novel_classes()` uses “any member similar to any previous finding” to mark the whole current class non-novel. This creates bridge effects and order-sensitive semantic collapse: one weakly-linked member can cause a whole heterogeneous class to be treated as old, hiding genuinely new findings.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compare equivalence classes to prior equivalence classes rather than flattening to raw findings, or compute novelty per member / per subcluster, or use complete-linkage / centroid matching to reduce bridge contamination.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

F014  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: `RoundProgressionFSM.select_event()` can return `Event.MAX` only when `round_complete` is true and current state is `ROUND_k` with `k == max_round_idx`. This implies the system must enter the last round and complete it before max-round termination fires. That is consistent internally, but the class docs say states are `{BLIND, SYNTH, ROUND_1, ..., ROUND_{N-1}, TERMINAL}` and “terminates in at most N + 2 transitions”; however with `max_rounds=1`, `max_round_idx=0`, the FSM still permits `BLIND -> SYNTH -> COMPLETE -> ROUND_1`, exceeding the documented round set.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Clarify whether `max_rounds` counts BLIND/SYNTH or only iterative rounds, and enforce lower bound / state construction consistently. If `max_rounds=1` means no iterative rounds, disallow `SYNTH -> ROUND_1`; if it means one iterative round, document states accordingly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F015  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.validate_no_findings()` docstring says “Convention: not converged unless null_expected,” but the implementation only checks `kappa_set(2) == 1.0` and does not test `converged()`. In actual code, if adoption delta is 0 and no veto occurs, `converged(2)` may become true once `kappa_rate` also saturates suitably. The validator therefore does not verify the stated convention and the implementation may contradict it.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Decide intended semantics for zero-findings runs and encode them explicitly in `converged()`. Update validator to check the actual predicate.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F016  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54  
DESCRIPTION: Multiple comments claim the ascending abstraction guard is implemented conjunctively in Area 5, but `DiminishingReturnsDetector.stop()` ignores abstraction entirely. `_abstraction_dropping()` exists and is unused. This is both a documentation mismatch and a latent logic omission relative to the stated design decision.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either implement the conjunctive guard in `stop()` (e.g. `smoothed_mu < tau_mu and abstraction_dropping and r>=r_min`) or revise comments/docstrings to state that abstraction is currently monitored but not used.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F017  
SEVERITY: 0.75  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.should_abort()` says “If only PM survives, framework degrades to single-model mode,” but the implemented condition is only `len(active_models) < k_min` with default `k_min=1`. That permits PM-only survival, but also permits non-PM-only survival if PM was never excluded from `_active_models`; however PM transport/protocol failures that lead to ABORT do not remove PM from `_active_models`, so the “if PM is not active, abort” branch may never trigger for PM hard failures unless exclusion happened separately.  
PROPOSED_FIX: On PM ABORT-worthy failure, explicitly mark PM inactive or have `should_abort()` consult failure state/termination reasons instead of active set alone. Align docs and logic.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F018  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` always stores `allocation=None` in `RoundResult`, despite `RoundResult` documenting cross-area communication and the caller likely needing allocation context for analysis. This weakens the orchestration interface and loses provenance needed for debugging cost/yield/failure decisions.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Accept allocation as an argument to `process_round()` and persist it in `RoundResult`, or store the most recent allocation inside `DynamicManager` before dispatch.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F019  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `Allocation.get_assigned_models()` and `get_assigned_tasks()` use `.index()` on ID lists and will raise `ValueError` for unknown IDs. For an orchestration layer, this is a brittle interface with poor diagnostics and O(n) lookup cost.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Precompute ID→index maps inside `Allocation`, validate uniqueness, and raise clearer errors or return empty sets as appropriate.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F020  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 7  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` repeatedly does `next((m for m in self._models if m.model_id == mid), None)` inside a loop, making reassignment O(K^2). Similar linear scans occur elsewhere. For small K this is acceptable, but the module repeatedly claims callable production implementation, and these avoidable scans accumulate across rounds.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Store a `model_id -> ModelSpec` dict in `RoleAssignment` and use direct lookup.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F021  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.kappa_rate()` bases normalization on round 1 if present, else round 0. If round 1 has zero classes and later rounds have findings, `rate_1 + epsilon_conv` becomes tiny and `kappa_rate` becomes a very large negative number before clamping. This causes unstable behavior and makes convergence depend heavily on whether round numbering included an empty round 1.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use the first non-zero reference rate or a more stable baseline estimate. At minimum, explicitly handle zero-reference cases.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F022  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._objective()` and `_balanced()` treat models with `L <= 0` as fraction 0.0 in vectorized `np.where`, while `Allocation.model_load_fraction()` returns `inf` if `L <= 0` and load > 0. These functions disagree on the meaning of zero-capacity models, creating inconsistent optimization vs reporting behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use the same convention everywhere; `inf` is more appropriate for positive load on zero capacity. Reject zero/negative capacities at config/model validation if unsupported.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F023  
SEVERITY: 0.70  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` updates fingerprints only when the FSM is not terminal. That means the final round’s observed performance is never incorporated into the live fingerprint history, creating a silent truncation of adaptive learning and inconsistent per-round metrics. If post-run analytics or warm-starting future runs depend on final fingerprints, they will be stale.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Update fingerprints for every processed round, or separate “update analytics state” from “use updated state for next allocation.”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F024  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: The module docstring claims “all six areas ... are implemented as callable classes and functions matching the interface contracts,” but several advertised features are partial/inert: feasibility is not enforced, correlated failure model is not integrated into failure handling or allocation, abstraction guard is unused. This overstates completeness.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Downgrade documentation claims or complete integration points so the public description matches behavior.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F025  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.65  
DESCRIPTION: The correlated failure model is completely disconnected from the rest of the management layer. `DynamicManager` instantiates it, but no scheduling, redundancy, abort, or risk decision consults it. As implemented, it is an auxiliary utility, not an Area 6 extension affecting system behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Integrate independence/correlation into allocation redundancy decisions, failure escalation, or dispatch diversification policy. Otherwise move it to a utility module and document it as advisory only.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F026  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` appends to `_perf_history` on every non-empty, non-timeout, parseable, format-compliant response, including responses from inactive/excluded models if passed in. There is no guard to ignore models outside `_active_models`. That can corrupt underperformance history after exclusion.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Ignore or reject responses from inactive models in `detect_failure()`, or enforce orchestration-side filtering before calling it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F027  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.51  
DESCRIPTION: `Task.flaw_class` and `Finding.flaw_class` are both plain integers with no validation or shared enum/type. The code assumes semantic comparability across tasks/findings, but nothing enforces a common taxonomy, making equivalence and coverage metrics fragile.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Introduce a shared enum or validated taxonomy object for flaw classes.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

F028  
SEVERITY: 0.65  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44  
DESCRIPTION: `ManagerEventStream.emit()` invokes callback synchronously with no exception handling. A faulty callback can break core management logic during failure detection or round processing. In orchestration layers, observability hooks should not normally be able to crash the control plane unless explicitly desired.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Catch and route callback exceptions, or make failure propagation configurable.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F029  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 3  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.38  
DESCRIPTION: `State.round_state(k)` returns a `str`, while `State` itself is an enum and `current_state` is also a `str`. This mixed representation weakens type safety and forces string parsing like `s.startswith("ROUND_")` and `int(s.split("_")[1])`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Represent round states with a dedicated dataclass/tuple or separate enum plus index, avoiding ad hoc string encoding.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F030  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.45  
DESCRIPTION: `blind_first` is documented as “HARD: always start with blind round” but is configurable and unused. The FSM always starts in BLIND regardless of the setting, so the parameter is dead and misleading.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove `blind_first`, or enforce/validate it as always `True`, or make the FSM actually consult it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F031  
SEVERITY: 0.62  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.53  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` records failures but emits no recovery-action events (`RETRY`, `EXCLUDE`, `ABORT`, etc.) despite `ManagerEventType` defining them and comments promising real-time manager monitoring of recovery actions. Only detection events are emitted.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit a `ManagerEvent` after action selection/recording for each recovery action.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F032  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.assign()` uses deterministic sorting with tuple key `(score, tie_break_key)` and `reverse=True`. If all fingerprints are identical, the final order depends on original input order because Python sort is stable and the keys are identical. The validator tolerates this, but the docs imply deterministic tie-breaking from capability attributes alone. Input-order dependence may be undesirable.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a final deterministic tiebreaker such as `model_id`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F033  
SEVERITY: 0.60  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.50  
DESCRIPTION: `DiminishingReturnsDetector.smoothed_marginal_value()` drops infinite `mu` values from zero-cost positive-yield rounds. This can lower the smoothed estimate in a way inconsistent with the documented “free information always worth having” handling in `marginal_value()`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define explicit smoothing semantics for infinite values, e.g. cap at large finite constant or short-circuit to `inf` if any recent round had free positive yield.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F034  
SEVERITY: 0.59  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.estimate_gamma()` returns `inf` when `cum_r == cum_1`, which may happen both under true convergence and under no-findings edge cases. As a diagnostic this is mathematically arguable, but operationally it conflates distinct scenarios and is not documented as such.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Distinguish “no growth” from “undefined due to zero/constant counts” with explicit sentinel handling or richer return type.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

F035  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41  
DESCRIPTION: Several validators use `assert` internally (`RoundProgressionFSM.validate_k1`, `FailureHandler.validate_k1`), which can be stripped with Python optimization flags, altering behavior of the self-test harness.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace `assert` with explicit conditional checks returning `False` or raising controlled exceptions.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F036  
SEVERITY: 0.57  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` computes `mu` using direct access to private state `self.diminishing_returns._cumulative_yields` in a redundant guard immediately after adding the round. This is not just style: it bypasses encapsulation and suggests uncertainty about detector invariants.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Call `marginal_value(round_idx)` directly after `add_round_from_findings()` or expose a safe `has_round()` method.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F037  
SEVERITY: 0.56  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.59  
DESCRIPTION: No uniqueness validation exists for `model_id`, `task_id`, or `finding_id`. Duplicate IDs would cause silent overwrites in dicts, ambiguous indexing, and corrupted metrics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate uniqueness on manager/load-balancer/convergence-detector entry points.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F038  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.48  
DESCRIPTION: `update_fingerprints()` claims “Every model that produced output gets updated,” but iterates over `self.failure_handler.active_models`, not models present in `responses`. An active model with missing response gets a synthetic no-findings fingerprint penalty; an inactive model with a late valid response is ignored. The implementation is policy-laden and not reflected in docs.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Decide whether updates are keyed by active-set membership or actual response receipt, and document/implement consistently.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F039  
SEVERITY: 0.54  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.36  
DESCRIPTION: The code imports many unused typing symbols (`Literal`, `Protocol`, `Union`, etc.). This is minor but indicates interface plans not realized in code.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove unused imports or implement the intended protocols/types.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F040  
SEVERITY: 0.53  
FLAW_CLASS: 7  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.42  
DESCRIPTION: `_finding_similarity()` uses naive whitespace splitting and raw Jaccard overlap. Punctuation/casing variants, stemming, and synonyms are untreated, making equivalence detection brittle and potentially expensive O(n^2 * text) across rounds.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Normalize tokens more robustly and/or allow pluggable preprocessing. For scale, use embeddings or MinHash/LSH for candidate pruning.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

F041  
SEVERITY: 0.52  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager` emits `ROUND_COMPLETE` at the start of `process_round()` before any processing, then emits another `ROUND_COMPLETE` from `update_fingerprints()`. The event taxonomy lacks a distinct “processing started” or “fingerprints updated” type, so consumers receive semantically overloaded duplicate events.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add distinct event types such as `ROUND_PROCESSING_START` and `FINGERPRINTS_UPDATED`, or emit `ROUND_COMPLETE` only once.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F042  
SEVERITY: 0.51  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44  
DESCRIPTION: `_admissibility_mask()` computes `k_total` as count of entries in `role_map` whose role is in `(PM, COL, PAR)`. Since those are the only roles, `k_total` is effectively `len(role_map)`, which may differ from `len(self.models)` if stale/mismatched role maps are passed. This makes PM inclusion depend on role-map completeness rather than actual model pool size.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base the K=1 special case on `len(self.models)` or on active modeled candidates intersected with role map explicitly. Validate alignment between `role_map` and `models`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F043  
SEVERITY: 0.50  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.40  
DESCRIPTION: `CorrelatedFailureModel.set_vulnerability()` allows `model_i == model_j`, storing a frozenset of one element. `get_vulnerability()` special-cases identical IDs to return 1.0, so self-set values are ignored and the internal store can contain meaningless entries.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reject self-pairs in `set_vulnerability()`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F044  
SEVERITY: 0.49  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46  
DESCRIPTION: `correlated_class_failure()` documentation says it uses “a conservative upper bound based on pairwise correlations” and references scaling by remaining probabilities, but the implementation simply computes `independent_all + max_correlation_boost`. The implemented formula does not match the documented one.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either revise the documentation to describe the actual heuristic or implement the stated scaling method.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F045  
SEVERITY: 0.48  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.33  
DESCRIPTION: Several comments reference external consensus provenance (“CC2 proposed...”, “2/3 agreement...”), which is not actionable for maintainers and clutters operational code.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Move provenance/rationale to design docs and keep code comments focused on invariant/algorithm explanation.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

F046  
SEVERITY: 0.47  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.39  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer.validate_homogeneous()` claims equal distribution should be balanced, but with PM excluded when `k>1`, homogeneous balance is constrained by one model being unavailable. The validator can still pass for its specific setup, but the property statement is overbroad and not generally true.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Narrow the validator/documentation to “balanced among admissible workers” or include COL/PAR-only pool.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F047  
SEVERITY: 0.45  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.37  
DESCRIPTION: `Finding.verified` is used as a proxy for verification quality in fingerprint updates, but no source-of-truth or verification provenance is modeled. A caller can set it arbitrarily, causing routing adaptation on untrusted metadata.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Represent verification provenance explicitly or keep this metric advisory and document trust assumptions.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

F048  
SEVERITY: 0.44  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` only emits events for EMPTY/TIMEOUT/MALFORMED/FORMAT and not for UNDERPERFORM, despite `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` existing. This creates observability blind spots for one of the five failure types.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit `UNDERPERFORM` events when the persistence criterion triggers.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

F049  
SEVERITY: 0.43  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.34  
DESCRIPTION: The `DynamicManagementConfig` docstring says “All values are SOFT parameters unless noted otherwise,” but some are effectively structural invariants (`max_rounds`, `blind_first`, maybe `k_min`) and code treats some comments as HARD without enforcement. The hardness model is not reflected in interfaces.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Separate protocol invariants from tunable thresholds into different config objects or annotate/validate immutable HARD values.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

F050  
SEVERITY: 0.42
